$comment: The declared inventory of this storefront's imagery.
Files live here, under brand/assets/. `npm run build` (and dev and preview)
mirrors this directory into public/assets/ before Astro runs, so public/assets/
is generated output and is gitignored. Editing a file under public/ is editing
a build artefact; it will be overwritten.
Every entry in `required` is exactly that: the sync fails the build when a
declared file is missing, rather than shipping a page with a broken image.
Drop an entry to make its file optional. Files present here but not declared
are still copied — the manifest is a floor, not a whitelist.
Alt text lives in brand/copy.ts next to the copy that renders it, not here.
Everything shipped is a neutral SVG placeholder. Replace them with real
artwork at the sizes under `conventions` and delete nothing else.

conventions.format: webp or jpg for photography, svg for marks and placeholders

$comment: SVGs allowed to name their own colours. Everything else under brand/assets/
must paint with currentColor (or none), and take its colour from a token at
the render site — see audit-color.mjs and pitfall #5.
The buckets are for readers, not for the audit: it flattens them. Being in
the wrong one is a review comment, not a build failure.
artwork          a picture standing in for photography. It has colours for
the same reason a photograph does; a real .jpg replaces it.
thirdPartyMarks  somebody else's logo. LINE green is LINE's, not the shop's,
and must NOT follow a rebrand.
wordmark         this shop's own mark, and the favicon and OG card built from
it. A favicon has nothing to inherit a colour from.
Files whose JOB is to be a stand-in, and which a shop is therefore not
expected to replace: the neutral squares src/lib/product-image.ts falls back
to when the catalogue has no photograph for a product.
They carry the same template-placeholder marker as everything else — they
ARE placeholders — so the sync would name them on every build of a perfectly
finished shop. A warning that fires when nothing is wrong is a warning
people learn to scroll past, which costs the ones that mean something.
Deleting them is not the alternative: a product added tomorrow with no image
would render a broken instead of a grey square.
